question: to the Commission Tobiasz Bocheński (ECR) Subject:

The European Parliament adopted its resolution of 13 September 2022 on responsible private funding of litigation1 with a large majority, calling on the Commission to introduce a harmonised regulatory framework for third-party litigation funding (TPLF). The volume of mass litigation is rising strongly and recent legislative developments, including the revised Product Liability Directive (PLD)2 and the Representative Actions Directive (RAD)3, will further increase litigation exposure for companies, including small and mediumsized enterprises, in the EU. The Commission’s study of 21 March 2025 entitled ‘Mapping Third Party Litigation Funding in the European Union’ confirms the rapid development of the multi-billion euro TPLF market and identifies transparency gaps, risks of conflicts of interest and divergent regulatory approaches in the Member States. 1.

Will the Commission issue guidance to ensure consistent PLD implementation by Member States and prevent unintended results, such as a reversal of the burden of proof, in order to protect EU competitiveness and the single market?

Despite broad support from Parliament for EU-level regulation of TPLF, why has the Commission not yet proposed any initiative on governance, transparency or financial oversight for litigation funders?

How does the Commission evaluate the combined effects of the new PLD, collective redress (RAD), and TPLF growth on legal certainty, insurance, compliance costs and EU competitiveness and simplification?

European Parliament resolution of 13 September 2022 with recommendations to the Commission on Responsible private funding of litigation (OJ C 125, 5.4.2023, p. 2). Directive (EU) 2024/2853 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC (OJ L, 2024/2853, 18.11.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2853/oj). Directive (EU) 2020/1828 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on representative actions for the protection of the collective interests of consumers and repealing Directive 2009/22/EC (OJ L 409, 4.12.2020, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2020/1828/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.5.2026) The Commission is monitoring the interaction between Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on Product Liability (PLD), the Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on Representative Actions (RAD) and developments in third-party litigation funding (TPLF), including their implications for legal certainty, costs and the internal market. The PLD strikes a careful balance between innovation and consumer protection. The Commission does not plan to issue specific guidelines but supports consistent implementation through cooperation with Member States, expert meetings, bilateral exchanges and transposition checks. In March 2025, the Commission published a study on TPLF1 which served as a basis for discussions with the European Parliament, the Member States and stakeholders in the HighLevel Forum on Justice for Growth. TPLF remains limited overall and does not reveal systemic risks. Participants expressed scepticism about the need for regulation and invited the Commission to continue monitoring developments, while assessing whether further action may be warranted. Under Article 23 of RAD, the Commission will evaluate its application by June 2028 in line with the 2030 Consumer Agenda and action plan for consumers in the single market.2 This evaluation will allow the Commission to determine whether further measures are necessary. It is therefore premature to draw conclusions on the combined effects of these legal instruments.
